messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 streaming latency > SLO in eu-west (SSE gateway). Metric: streaming.tail_p99 = 2.4s (SLO 1.2s). triggered at 2025-08-14T10:03:20Z
ara-oncall: saw it, paging in. I'm oncall for this window. starting triage.
derek-sre: joining — any customer  impact yet?
ara-oncall: looks like increased chunk delays and some clients reporting stalled streams. top affected route: /v1/stream/generate (eu-west).
mina-runtime: noticing a pattern: gateway keepalive spikes + proxy write timeouts. backend runtime p95 okay, but gateway p99 shoots up.
paul-sre: can you paste the query that triggered the alert? need the grafana panel link
ara-oncall: grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/streams/streaming-latency?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west
ara-oncall: timeline: spike started ~10:02:40Z, peaked at 10:03:15Z, now plateauing but above SLO
derek-sre: running quick look at streaming gateway logs for that minute. grep for 2025-08-14T10:02
ops-bot: deploy-bot: A canary rollout (gateway:v2.8.1 -> v2.9.0) started 2025-08-14T09:59:30Z in eu-west-1, 20% traffic.
mina-runtime: interesting — maybe the new gateway change interacts with keepalive/backpressure heuristics. pulling gateway logs now.
ara-oncall: mitigation idea: route eu-west traffic to fallback pool (gateway:v2.8.1) while we triage. canary rollback?
derek-sre: agree. initiating traffic shift to stable pool (arn:gw-eu-west-stable). I'll run the routing command.
paul-sre: +1. also add temporary rule to increase upstream write timeout from 30s -> 60s to reduce client disconnect churn.
ara-oncall: Derek, paste the command so I can ack and monitor.
derek-sre: running: ```
# shift 50% traffic back to stable pool
redwoodctl routing set --region eu-west --service gateway --target stable --split 50
```
derek-sre: done. split now 70/30 stable/canary. monitoring.
mina-runtime: extracting a snippet from gateway logs — lots of repeated ``TCP_WRITE_TIMEOUT`` entries right before p99 spike: ```
[2025-08-14T10:02:58Z] gw-23 write_timeout conn_id=0x7fae3a client=10.20.5.12 route=/v1/stream/generate status=partial
[2025-08-14T10:03:03Z] gw-23 write_timeout conn_id=0x7fae3a client=10.20.5.12 route=/v1/stream/generate status=partial
```
ara-oncall: are clients marked slow-consumer? any evidence of downstream backpressure from ALB?
mina-runtime: ALB metrics show increased backend_5xx? No, 5xx stable. but target_conn_active rising then dropping -> suggests clients dropping connections.
paul-sre: that matches proxy timeouts: gateway attempts to flush chunk but client hasn't acked, so write blocks until timeout. When timeout triggers, we close and re-establish -> tail latency increases.
derek-sre: rollback full canary to stable to confirm: ```
redwoodctl routing set --region eu-west --service gateway --target stable --split 100
```
derek-sre: applied. canary = 0%.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Traffic rerouted: gateway:v2.9.0 -> 0% in eu-west; v2.8.1 -> 100% as of 2025-08-14T10:04:01Z.
ara-oncall: monitoring p99 now...
mina-runtime: p99 dropped from 2.4s -> 1.1s in next 30s. looks like rollback addressed the spike.
paul-sre: good. next: postmortem steps and root cause. preliminary hypothesis: canary introduced subtle change in socket write behavior (keepalive / buffering) that exacerbates slow-client backpressure and caused write timeouts.
derek-sre: capturing logs for the canary instances for deeper diff. pulling tcpdump from gw-canary nodes.
ara-oncall: customer impact? any support tickets flagged?
mina-runtime: one customer (acct: 98765) reported stalled stream in EU at 10:03Z; they retried and resumed. no major outages reported.
paul-sre: impact severity: P2 (partial degradation, user-retriable). recommend customer comms: short note to affected accounts.
ara-oncall: putting a short blurb in status: "We observed intermittent streaming stalls in EU region between 10:02-10:05 UTC due to a gateway canary. Traffic has been reverted to stable. We’re investigating"
paul-sre: I'll own the incident writeup and RCA. Derek & Mina, please add logs/traces and kernel/tcp settings diff.
derek-sre: will do. grabbing kernel tcp_* metrics from canary vs stable (send/rcv buffers, tcp_writeq_len).
mina-runtime: also triage client idle timeout handling — the new gateway code touched write coalescing and flush thresholds. adding unit/integration test to reproduce slow-consumer scenario.
ara-oncall: next actions: 1) keep routing on stable until we finish RCA 2) run extended soak with synthetic slow-consumers on canary branch 3) prepare PR reverting the specific change if reproduced
ops-bot: pager-duty: paging cleared as mitigation is applied, monitoring for 15m.
ara-oncall: thanks team. I'll update status page and close this thread after 15m observation window if p99 stays < SLO. :thumbsup:
paul-sre: note for postmortem: include exact canary commit id, diff of write path, and any timeouts changed.
derek-sre: cc: @sre-oncall-runbook — might be worth updating runbook to include quick rollback steps for gateway canaries.
mina-runtime: adding logs to the incident archive. exporting traces: ```
trace-id: 0x9f1a2b
span: gateway.write -> runtime.enqueue delay=120ms
```
ara-oncall: last check: p99 = 0.98s at 10:05:05Z. closing handoff in 10m if stable. good job.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: handoff to postmortem queue created (id: INC-2025-08214-01).
